The test arrived inside 24 hours, and it arrived in a harsher form than expected.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's story is about who actually controls a price. Start with the long end of the Treasury curve. On August nineteenth, Treasury surprised the market by at least doubling the size of its longer-dated bond buybacks.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the industry stopped arguing about whether AI demand is real and started arguing about dates. Across custom silicon, foundry, and Intel's own roadmap, commitment after commitment slid to the right. The one thing that did not slide is the memory bill. That's the spine of today's briefing.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past several days this show has closed on the same complaint. Three enterprise software vendors reported, three of them beat, and not one told you what share of its growth was actually artificial intelligence, in a unit an outsider could reason about.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Fair warning up front. This is a structural read, not a news day. The freshest thing on my desk closed three weeks ago, and I'll tell you the vintage of each piece of evidence as it arrives.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power spent the day on one question. Can Washington talk the thirty-year yield down by itself? Treasury doubled the size of its long-dated bond buybacks. It was also reported to be weighing its roughly nine-hundred-fifty-billion-dollar cash account as extra ammunition.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — August 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the one that resolved, with an asterisk I am putting on it myself. Yesterday I said the US spot bitcoin funds would record at least one net-outflow day within two weeks, at about three-in-four.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Backdrop first, briefly, because we led on it Saturday and it is scenery today rather than news. Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on Friday the 28th pushed September hike odds from roughly 35 percent to somewhere near 60. That range moves with every CME snapshot, so hold it loosely.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a quick bridge, because this show covered Friday's shock in full over the weekend. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave a hawkish Jackson Hole speech. Traders repriced the odds of a September rate hike from roughly 35 percent to about 60 percent.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a reversal. On the metric of gas-fired power capacity under development, the United States has passed China, and data centers are why. The Global Energy Monitor's August report puts it plainly.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has called memory the one input cost in this industry that refuses to slide while every revenue commitment moves right. Today brings the first supply-side answer to that constraint, and it is not the answer anyone was hoping for.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: For a month, this beat has watched cheap agent tokens arrive with expiry dates stapled to them. OpenAI's discount on its flagship model is promotional and lapses on a published date. Google's agent pricing is the same shape. Neither lab is lowering prices, as this show has argued. Both are renting habits.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Here is the fact that has not aired on this show yet. Claude is now the default model inside Slack. Not an option, not a plugin you switch on — the default, powering Slackbot and a new feature called Claude Tag for team decision-making. Alongside it, Salesforce shipped something called Salesforce in Claude.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start from the two facts that frame everything else. No AI-designed medicine has been approved by any regulator in any major market. And no layer of the stack has yet moved the failure rate that actually costs money, which is Phase II. Today the first AI-native drug company to turn a real profit reported its numbers.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Three briefings running, this beat has been handed its biggest numbers by the people those numbers flatter. Today the largest number yet arrives at the layer underneath everything. Not the machine — the model. It is worth slowing down on.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: This show has spent the past week showing you private-equity assets priced by whoever controls the sale. Inside the fund, through continuation vehicles. At the allocator, when a pension declines to roll.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has the reversal of the year on gas. The United States now has twice as much gas-fired capacity in development as China, and the slice tied directly to data centers nearly doubled in six months, to 189 gigawatts.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — August 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and start with the one going against me. On Saturday I called high-yield credit spreads above three hundred basis points before the September sixteenth Fed meeting, at about two-in-five.
